svg.aria-label: The advanced filter URL rendered as visible text wrapped to two lines, with the five URL parts as hoverable regions and the three new query parameters rendered in copper.
svg.title: Greenfield's advanced filter URL with five hoverable parts
svg.desc: The URL https://api.greenfield.lib/v1/books?q=mystery&branch=branch_north&shelf=fiction&on_shelf=true wrapped to two lines. Line 1 carries the scheme (https), host (api.greenfield.lib), version (/v1), and resource (/books). Line 2 carries the query string with q=mystery in ink and the three new query parameters (branch, shelf, on_shelf) in copper. Hovering or tapping each part reveals what it commits to and who reads it downstream.
svg.text: The advanced filter URL. Hover or tap each part.

g.data-tooltip: The protocol the client speaks. HTTPS means encrypted. Every byte after the :// is unreadable to anything in the middle. Greenfield is HTTPS like every public API a 2026 reader is calling.
What DNS resolves to an IP address. The api. subdomain separates the API server from Greenfield's public site at greenfield.lib. Two different machines, same registered domain.
The version segment Devon put in the URL on day one. When Greenfield ships v2, /v1 keeps working until Devon turns it off. Some APIs hide the version in a header. Devon keeps it visible.
The noun. The handler that serves this URL is the books handler. The query string changes which books come back; the resource decides the response is about books in the first place.

g.aria-label: query string: ?q=mystery and three new params
g.data-tooltip: Four name=value pairs separated by &. The first, q=mystery, was already there. You added branch, shelf, and on_shelf this morning. The query string parameterizes the handler. Same handler, different filter.
